concept.title: Writing style guidelines
concept.abstract: This chapter defines writing and editorial standards for DITA content, covering voice, tone, grammar, command authoring, short descriptions, UI references, and punctuation conventions. It explains how structured writing principles improve consistency, usability, localization, and searchability while aligning DITA content with industry-recognized style guides such as Microsoft, Google, IBM, CMOS, and S1000D/ASD-STE100. The chapter establishes a framework for creating clear, action-oriented, and standards-compliant technical documentation across diverse industries and publishing environments.

conbody.p: When authoring in DITA, technical writers must adhere to the Microsoft Style Guide for Technical Publication or the specified style guide for their organization. Here are some general writing guidelines when authoring in DITA.
